title: Grade 8 Science — Mon, Jun 01
description: Synthetic Fibres & Plastics — Day 1 of 5: What are synthetic fibres?
subject: science

questions.question: Synthetic fibres are made by humans from raw materials obtained mainly from:
questions.explanation: Synthetic fibres are man-made from chemicals called petrochemicals, obtained from petroleum.

questions.question: A synthetic fibre is made of many small repeating units joined together to form a large molecule called a:
questions.explanation: A polymer is a large molecule made of many small repeating units called monomers.

questions.question: The first fully synthetic fibre made by humans was:
questions.explanation: Nylon, made in 1931, was the first fully synthetic fibre, made without any natural raw material.

questions.question: Rayon is called a 'semi-synthetic' fibre because it is made from:
options: Wood pulp (a natural source) treated with chemicals
questions.explanation: Rayon is obtained from wood pulp, a natural material, treated with chemicals — so it is semi-synthetic.

questions.question: Rayon is also known as:
questions.explanation: Because it has a silky look and is cheaper, rayon is called artificial silk.

questions.question: Which fibre is known for being very strong, elastic and used in parachutes and ropes?
questions.explanation: Nylon is strong and elastic, so it is used in parachutes, ropes, seat belts and toothbrush bristles.

questions.question: Polyester is a synthetic fibre that:
options: Does not wrinkle easily and is easy to wash
questions.explanation: Polyester resists wrinkles and dries quickly, making it popular for clothes.

questions.question: PET, used to make bottles and many containers, is a type of:
questions.explanation: PET (polyethylene terephthalate) is a kind of polyester used for bottles, jars and films.

questions.question: Acrylic is a synthetic fibre that looks and feels like:
questions.explanation: Acrylic resembles wool and is used to make sweaters and blankets, often cheaper than real wool.

questions.question: Synthetic fibres are popular because they are cheaper, durable and:
questions.explanation: Synthetic fibres are inexpensive, strong, readily available and dry fast.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a synthetic fibre?
questions.explanation: Cotton is a natural plant fibre; nylon, polyester and acrylic are synthetic.

questions.question: The small repeating unit that joins to form a polymer is called a:
questions.explanation: Monomers are the small units that link together to make a polymer.

questions.question: Natural fibres like cotton and wool are also polymers. For example, cotton is made of the polymer:
questions.explanation: Cotton is made of cellulose, a natural polymer, showing polymers occur in nature too.

questions.question: Why is rayon mixed with cotton to make bedsheets?
options: To combine the qualities of both fibres
questions.explanation: Mixing fibres combines useful qualities — rayon adds silkiness and cotton adds comfort.

questions.question: Which statement about synthetic fibres is TRUE?
options: They are obtained directly from plants
They are man-made polymers, often from petrochemicals
They are dug out of the ground
questions.explanation: Synthetic fibres are man-made polymers, usually produced from petrochemicals.
